summary: Pasadena ISD argues that E‑Rate remains necessary, broadband prices have fallen, and the district has largely exhausted its Category Two budget; it requests removal of the 85 % discount ceiling, maintenance of dark‑fiber eligibility, and other administrative changes. Pasadena ISD argues that the current 85 % Category Two discount ceiling forces the district to pay more than it would under a 90 % discount, resulting in unnecessary local cost and requests a change to the discount rate. Pasadena ISD argues for more equitable discount rates, expanded eligible services, greater transparency in selective review, and limited dark‑fiber support. Pasadena ISD argues that special construction and maintenance/operation of leased dark fiber should remain eligible under E‑Rate, that a national per‑foot or per‑strand cap is inappropriate, and that the FCC should not impose a categorical bidding requirement without reviewing data. Pasadena ISD argues for more flexible pricing rules, stronger enforcement against bid steering and fraud, and clearer guidance on substitution approvals and delivery deadlines. Pasadena ISD argues that district‑run pre‑kindergarten should remain eligible for E‑Rate funding and that E‑Rate funding should not be conditioned on screen‑time limits or parental opt‑outs. Pa
